narrative:
The model has predicted a 23% chance that you will fail your final year, which is above the threshold that indicates you must take remedial courses. This means that, based on the data analyzed, there are several factors that suggest you may struggle academically unless additional support is provided.

The most influential factor in this prediction is your father's education level, which is at the primary level. This suggests that there may be less academic support available at home compared to students whose parents have higher education. Additionally, while you have not had any past failures, your weekly study time of 2-5 hours is lower than many of your peers, who often study more. This indicates that you might not be dedicating enough time to your studies, which can impact your understanding of the material.

Lastly, the absence of extra educational support, such as tutoring or additional classes, further contributes to the prediction. Most students in similar situations receive some form of extra help, which you currently do not. 

Given these insights, it is crucial for you to engage in remedial courses. These courses will provide you with the necessary support to strengthen your understanding of the subjects and improve your chances of passing. It’s also advisable to consider increasing your study time and seeking additional resources or support to enhance your learning experience.
